creator: bengusberg
title: Promotes 'Unlazy', a free anti-laziness skill (Depth Tree method) that makes Claude/ChatGPT split tasks into subtasks so it stops skipping steps

tools.name: Unlazy
tools.detail: Free skill; invoked as '/unlazy' at the start of a project; GitHub 'About' says 'Anti-laziness skill for AI agents. Core: the Depth Tree method'

claims: Anthropic and OpenAI 'designed their latest models to be lazy, cut corners, and lie that the job is done' (framing; official term given as 'partial compliance')
Fix takes '20 seconds or less' to install
Unlazy forces the model to split tasks into subtasks and give each the full time to complete
Creator intro: Stanford founder of an AI startup that raised $4 million
how_to_steps: Go to the Unlazy website/repo (URL not legible in frames)
Copy the URL into Claude or ChatGPT and tell it to help you install the skill
When starting a project, type /unlazy so the task is split into sub-tasks each given full effort
on_screen_only: Snippet: 'Partial compliance in AI occurs when an artificial intelligence system or its provider satisfies some—but not all—regulatory, safety, or operational requirements'

GitHub About box: 'Anti-laziness skill for AI agents. Core: the Depth Tree method, which splits a task N layers deep and gives every leaf the full time budget of the whole task, so effort multiplies with depth. Grounded in 2025–2026 research on model laziness, underthinking and premature completion.'
cta: Try it and let me know what you build; follow for more

relevance.why: Premature 'done' claims from agents are a real pain for a solo founder reviewing Claude Code output; a skill that forces decomposition and per-leaf effort is relevant, though the repo/author is not named.

implement_score.why: Cheap to trial as a Claude Code skill if the repo is real; the underlying idea (make Claude write a task tree and verify each leaf before declaring done) can also be done with a short CLAUDE.md rule in 10 minutes.

verify: Find the actual Unlazy repo and author; is it maintained and what does the skill file actually contain?
Does the 'Depth Tree' approach blow up token cost/time on simple tasks?
Is the 'models designed to be lazy' framing supported by anything, or just the hook?
